"Arguing that you don’t care about the right to privacy because you have nothing to hide is no different than saying you don’t care about free speech because you have nothing to say," -Edward Snowden

Another reason this widely-held position is absurd is that people routinely underestimate what is "personal or sensitive" and the fact that what should be considered personal or sensitive often only becomes apparent in retrospect.

This can be especially true with Governments who make things illegal retroactively.

Also, let's assume that you suddenly did have a secure message that you wanted to send. It's foolish to simply encrypt only secure messages - you are then doing the hard work for spooks by sorting out interesting and important messages. It's the same flaw with only shredding secure documents. If you want to shred documents securely, you need to shred a lot of unimportant paper too so that the good stuff is a needle in a haystack.

So, my advice is to encrypt everything - just in case someday you suddenly need security. It's harder to get security when you need it if you haven't protected it when you didn't.
